tutorial.title: Creating Grid Columns
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to create grid columns

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent: Let's set the size and number of grid columns. Press the buttons to see how CSS Grid lays out a simple game HUD with different slot counts.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
To define grid columns that have a fixed size, we use pixels. Code 100px, 50px and 100px to make a game HUD with panels of different widths.

Make sure to pick 100px, followed by 50px, and finally 100px.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Grid items follow the column count. If there are more HUD items than columns, extra items move to the next row.

Make sure to pick <div class="grid-item">, followed by Ammo, and finally </div>.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's take a look at values that adapt to the screen size. Setting a column to auto will make HUD panels take up as much space as they can.

Make sure to pick auto.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
Grid has a special measurement unit called fr, short for fractional unit. fr distributes the container's available space in fractions.

Make sure to type fr.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we combine fr with other units like px, the space left after adding the px item is what gets distributed in fractions. Code 50px 1fr 1fr.

Make sure to pick 50px, followed by 1fr, and finally 1fr.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
Grid has a shortcut for defining columns quickly, and that's the repeat() function. For example, repeat(3, 1fr) means 3 equal HUD panels.

Make sure to pick repeat followed by ( and then 3, ,, 1fr, ).

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
What units should we use to define a fixed HUD grid column?

PixelsPercentages

Make sure to pick Pixels.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we have three HUD items but only define two columns with grid-template-columns?

The third item is sent to the next rowThe third item stays on the first row if there's enough space

The third item is sent to the next row.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which HUD column is the largest in size when we set grid-template-columns to 30% 30% 40%?

The third columnThe second column

The third column.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's true about the first and second HUD columns when we set grid-template-columns to 1fr 2fr?

The second column is twice the size the first columnThe first column is twice the size the second column

The second column is twice the size the first column.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we create HUD columns using the following code?

The remaining space on the right is evenly distributed across the last two columnsThe remaining space on the right is evenly distributed across the first two columns

The remaining space on the right is evenly distributed across the last two columns.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create three equal HUD grid columns using pixel values.

Make sure to pick grid-template-columns followed by 100px and then 100px, 100px.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add a fourth HUD grid item.

Make sure to pick < followed by div and then class="item", >, Ammo, </, div, >.

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a two-column HUD grid by coding 50% 50%.

Make sure to type 50% 50%.

lessons.title: Lesson #16
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a grid so that the first HUD column is half the width of the other columns.

Make sure to pick 1fr, followed by 2fr, and finally 2fr.

lessons.title: Lesson #17
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code 40px 1fr 1fr to distribute the remaining space to the second and third HUD columns.

Make sure to type 40px 1fr 1fr.

lessons.title: Lesson #18
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code 40px 1fr 3fr to distribute the remaining space to the second and third HUD columns in different proportions.

Make sure to pick 40px, followed by 1fr, and finally 3fr.

lessons.title: Lesson #19
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use the repeat() function to create two columns that are 2fr wide each (perfect for two big HUD panels).

Make sure to pick repeat followed by ( and then 2, ,, 2fr, ).
